content: Apple has no single guideline forbidding charging for user-created local data, but 3.1.2(a) (do not take away paid primary functionality when switching to subscription), 5.1.1(ii) (paid functionality must not depend on user data access), and Schedule 2 (users must retain access to content they created during a lapsed subscription for auto-renewables) create rejection risk for hard-locking local history. BabyLog's soft-gate (hide >24h, keep data, free Emergency 24h) is compliant-by-design; the danger is regression during implementation.
